onChange={e => setName(e.target.value)}

placeholder="Enter name"

/>

<button type="submit">Submit</button>

</form>

);

}

export default StudentForm;

Conclusion: The POST method allows React forms to send user information to a PHP backend.

q: Q40. Build a simple React app that displays user list fetched from MySQL via a PHP API.
a:
First, create a MySQL database named college and a table named users.

Create a PHP API that connects to MySQL and retrieves all user records.

Convert the retrieved records into JSON using json_encode().

In React, use fetch() to call the PHP API and useState() to store the response.

Display the user records using the map() function.

PHP API (users.php):

<?php

header("Content-Type: application/json");

$conn = new mysqli(

"localhost", "root", "", "college"

);

$result = $conn->query("SELECT * FROM users");

$users = [];

while ($row = $result->fetch_assoc()) {

$users[] = $row;

}

echo json_encode($users);

?>

React Code:

import { useEffect, useState } from "react";

function App() {

const [users, setUsers] = useState([]);

useEffect(() => {

fetch("http://localhost/api/users.php")

.then(res => res.json())

.then(data => setUsers(data));

}, []);

return users.map(user =>

<p key={user.id}>{user.name}</p>

);

}

export default App;

Conclusion: React, PHP, and MySQL work together to retrieve and display dynamic user information.

q: Q41. Create a deployable build of a React app and explain what happens in the build process.
a:
Develop Application: First, create a React project and write the required components, CSS, and JavaScript code.

Install Dependencies: Install all required packages using:

npm install

Create Build: Run the command:

npm run build

Build Process: The build tool converts source files into optimized production files, bundles JavaScript and CSS, and processes assets.

Deployment: The generated dist folder in Vite or build folder in Create React App contains files ready for hosting.

Conclusion: The React build process creates optimized production files that can be uploaded to a hosting platform.

q: Q42. Build a full cycle: React form → PHP API → MySQL → React display.
a:
React Form: Create a form to collect user information, such as name and email.

PHP API: Send the form data to PHP using the POST method. PHP validates and processes the information.

MySQL Database: PHP uses a prepared SQL statement to insert the information into MySQL.

Retrieve Data: PHP provides another API that fetches saved records and returns them in JSON format.

React Display: React calls the GET API and displays the saved records using map().

Example Flow:

React Form

Collects user information

PHP API

Validates and processes data

MySQL Database

Stores user information

React Display

Shows saved records

Conclusion: This complete cycle connects the frontend, backend, and database to create a dynamic web application.

q: Q43. Create a PHP API that returns JSON data from a MySQL database.
a:
A PHP API allows React applications to access database information.

First, PHP connects to the MySQL database using MySQLi.

An SQL SELECT query retrieves the required records.

The fetch_assoc() function converts database rows into associative arrays.

The json_encode() function converts the array into JSON format for React.

PHP Code (users.php):

<?php

header("Content-Type: application/json");

$conn = new mysqli(

"localhost", "root", "", "college"

);

if ($conn->connect_error) {

http_response_code(500);

echo json_encode(["error" => "Connection failed"]);

exit;

}

$sql = "SELECT id, name, email FROM users";

$result = $conn->query($sql);

$users = [];

while ($row = $result->fetch_assoc()) {

$users[] = $row;

}

echo json_encode($users);

$conn->close();

?>

Conclusion: A PHP API retrieves MySQL records and sends them to React in JSON format.

q: Q44. Create a React component that displays a loading message until API data is fetched.
a:
The useState() hook manages the API data and loading status.

Initially, the loading variable is set to true.

The useEffect() hook calls the API when the component loads.

When data is received, setData() stores the response and loading becomes false.

React displays the loading message until the data is successfully fetched.

React Code:

import { useEffect, useState } from "react";

function App() {

const [data, setData] = useState([]);

const [loading, setLoading] = useState(true);

useEffect(() => {

fetch("http://localhost/api/users.php")

.then(res => res.json())

.then(result => setData(result))

.catch(error => console.log(error))

.finally(() => setLoading(false));

}, []);

if (loading) {

return <h3>Loading...</h3>;

}

return (

<div>

<h2>User List</h2>

{data.map(user =>

<p key={user.id}>{user.name}</p>

)}

</div>

);

}

export default App;

Conclusion: Loading messages improve the user experience while React waits for API responses.

q: Q45. Design a React+PHP system where form entries are validated on both frontend and backend.
a:
Frontend Validation: React checks whether required fields are empty before submitting the form.

Input Checking: React can validate email format, password length, and other input requirements.

Backend Validation: PHP checks the submitted data again because frontend validation can be bypassed.

Database Security: PHP uses prepared statements to prevent SQL injection and stores only valid information.

Error Messages: PHP returns appropriate JSON responses, and React displays success or error messages.

React Example:

function validate(name, email) {

if (!name.trim()) return "Name is required";

if (!/^\S+@\S+\.\S+$/.test(email))

return "Invalid email";

return "";

}

PHP Example:

if (empty($_POST['name']) ||

!filter_var($_POST['email'], FILTER_VALIDATE_EMAIL)) {

http_response_code(400);

echo json_encode(["error" => "Invalid input"]);

exit;

}

Conclusion: Validating data on both frontend and backend improves application security and data accuracy.

q: Q46. Create a React search bar that filters data fetched from PHP API.
a:
First, create a PHP API that retrieves user records from the MySQL database.

React uses useEffect() to fetch the user data when the component loads.

The useState() hook stores the user list and search text.

The filter() function searches for matching names based on the entered text.

React displays only the matching records using the map() function.

React Code:

import { useEffect, useState } from "react";

function App() {

const [users, setUsers] = useState([]);

const [search, setSearch] = useState("");

useEffect(() => {

fetch("http://localhost/api/users.php")

.then(res => res.json())

.then(data => setUsers(data));

}, []);

const filtered = users.filter(user =>

user.name.toLowerCase().includes(search.toLowerCase())

);

return (

<div>

<input

placeholder="Search user"

value={search}

onChange={e => setSearch(e.target.value)}

/>

{filtered.map(user =>

<p key={user.id}>{user.name}</p>

)}

</div>

);

}

export default App;

Conclusion: A React search bar makes it easier to find specific records from API data.

q: Q47. Design a backend PHP script that accepts and returns JSON data with response status.
a:
A PHP backend can accept JSON data from React through an HTTP POST request.

The php://input stream reads the incoming JSON request body.

The json_decode() function converts JSON data into a PHP object.

PHP validates the received information and processes it according to application requirements.

The http_response_code() function sets the response status, while json_encode() returns JSON data.

PHP Code:

<?php

header("Content-Type: application/json");

$data = json_decode(

file_get_contents("php://input"),

true

);

if (!$data || empty($data['name'])) {

http_response_code(400);

echo json_encode([

"status" => "error",

"message" => "Name is required"

]);

exit;

}

http_response_code(200);

echo json_encode([

"status" => "success",

"message" => "Data received",

"name" => $data['name']

]);

?>

Conclusion: PHP can exchange JSON data with React and return suitable HTTP response statuses.

q: Q48. Build a system to send user feedback from a React app and store it in MySQL via PHP.
a:
React Form: Create a feedback form containing name, email, and message fields.

Submit Data: React sends the entered information to the PHP API using the POST method.

PHP Processing: PHP receives the information and validates all required fields.

Database Storage: PHP connects to MySQL and inserts feedback using a prepared statement.

Response: PHP returns a JSON success or error message, which React displays to the user.

PHP Example:

<?php

header("Content-Type: application/json");

$conn = new mysqli(

"localhost", "root", "", "college"

);

$name = $_POST['name'] ?? '';

$message = $_POST['message'] ?? '';

if (trim($name) === '' || trim($message) === '') {

http_response_code(400);

exit(json_encode(["message" => "Fields required"]));

}

$stmt = $conn->prepare(

"INSERT INTO feedback (name, message) VALUES (?, ?)"

);

$stmt->bind_param("ss", $name, $message);

$stmt->execute();

echo json_encode(["message" => "Feedback submitted"]);

?>

Conclusion: React, PHP, and MySQL provide a simple system for collecting and storing user feedback.

q: Q49. Create a complete deployment-ready build of a React frontend and integrate with existing PHP backend.
a:
Prepare React: Complete the React application and configure the PHP API URL using environment variables.

Create Build: Run npm install and npm run build to generate optimized production files.

Prepare PHP Backend: Ensure the PHP API is working correctly and the MySQL database connection is configured on the server.

Upload Files: Upload the generated dist folder contents to the web hosting directory and upload the PHP backend to its API directory.

Test Integration: Configure CORS, check API URLs, test database operations, and verify that React can communicate with PHP.

Example API URL:

const API_URL = "https://example.com/api/users.php";

fetch(API_URL)

.then(res => res.json())

.then(data => console.log(data));

Conclusion: A production build of React can be integrated with an existing PHP backend to create a complete web application.

q: Q50. Design a React component that fetches weather data from an external API and displays it.
a:
Create a React component that accepts a city name from the user.

Use an external weather API to retrieve temperature and weather conditions.

Use fetch() to send a request to the weather API.

Store the received weather information using the useState() hook.

Display the city name, temperature, and weather condition on the webpage.

React Code:

import { useState } from "react";

function Weather() {

const [city, setCity] = useState("");

const [weather, setWeather] = useState(null);

const getWeather = async () => {

const key = "YOUR_API_KEY";

const url =

`https://api.openweathermap.org/data/2.5/weather?q=${city}&appid=${key}&units=metric`;

const response = await fetch(url);

const data = await response.json();

if (response.ok) {

setWeather(data);

} else {

alert(data.message);

}

};

return (

<div>

<input

placeholder="Enter city"

onChange={e => setCity(e.target.value)}

/>

<button onClick={getWeather}>Search</button>

{weather && (

<div>

<h2>{weather.name}</h2>

<p>Temperature: {weather.main.temp} °C</p>

<p>{weather.weather[0].description}</p>

</div>

)}

</div>

);

}

export default Weather;

Conclusion: React can use external APIs to display real-time weather information dynamically.

q: Q2. Define Android technology.
a: Android is an open-source mobile operating system developed by Google. It is mainly used in smartphones, tablets, smart TVs and smartwatches. Android is based on the Linux kernel and supports different applications. Developers use Java and Kotlin to create Android apps. It provides features like internet access, camera, Bluetooth, GPS and multimedia support. Android allows users to download applications from the Google Play Store. It is popular because it is flexible, user-friendly and supports many devices.

q: Q3. List the main features of Android as a mobile operating system.
a:
Android has many useful features that make it a popular mobile operating system.

Open Source: Developers can modify Android according to their needs.
User-Friendly: It provides an easy and attractive interface.
Multitasking: Users can run multiple applications.
Connectivity: It supports Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, NFC and mobile networks.
Multimedia: It supports audio, video, camera and images.

Other features include GPS, notifications, security and application support.

q: Q4. Identify the main components of the Android architecture.
a:
Android architecture consists of five main layers.

Linux Kernel: Manages hardware, memory and device drivers.
Hardware Abstraction Layer (HAL): Connects hardware with software.
Android Runtime (ART): Runs Android applications.
Application Framework: Provides services like notifications and activity management.
Applications: Includes built-in and user-installed apps.

These layers work together to run Android applications smoothly. Android architecture makes application development easier, organized and efficient.

q: Q5. State the purpose of the Android SDK.
a: Android SDK stands for Software Development Kit. It is a collection of tools used to develop Android applications. Its main purpose is to help developers create, test and debug apps. It includes important tools like libraries, APIs, emulator and debugging tools. Developers use the SDK with Android Studio to build applications. It also provides documentation and sample code. The Android SDK makes application development easier and helps developers create apps for different Android devices.

q: Q6. Recognize the importance of Android in the mobile industry.
a:
Android plays an important role in the mobile industry because it is used by millions of people worldwide.

It supports smartphones and tablets.

It provides an open-source platform for developers.

It supports millions of applications.

It offers affordable devices from different companies.

It creates employment opportunities for developers.

Android also supports online banking, education, shopping and entertainment. Its flexibility and large user base make it an important mobile operating system.

q: Q7. Describe the process and purpose of mobile application development, mentioning the key steps and platforms used.
a:
Mobile application development is the process of creating applications for smartphones and tablets. Its main purpose is to provide useful services to users.

The main steps are:
Planning: Decide the app's purpose.
Design: Create the user interface.
Development: Write the application code.
Testing: Find and fix errors.
Deployment: Publish the application.

Popular platforms include Android Studio, Xcode and Flutter. These tools help developers create mobile applications easily.

q: Q8. Describe the role of Android Studio in app development.
a:
Android Studio is the official Integrated Development Environment (IDE) for Android application development. It provides tools to create, test and manage Android apps.

Its main features are:
Code Editor: Helps developers write code.
Layout Editor: Helps design app screens.
Emulator: Tests apps without a physical device.
Debugger: Finds and fixes errors.
Gradle: Manages building and dependencies.

Android Studio supports Java and Kotlin. It makes Android development easier and faster.

q: Q9. Explain the function of the Android Emulator.
a:
Android Emulator is a tool used to run Android applications on a computer without using a physical mobile device. It creates a virtual Android device.

Its main functions are:

It tests applications on a computer.

It supports different screen sizes.

It checks app performance.

It helps find and fix errors.

It supports different Android versions.

The emulator is included in Android Studio. It saves time and helps developers test applications safely.

q: Q10. Summarize the process of installing Android Studio.
a:
Android Studio is installed by following these simple steps.

Visit the official Android Studio website.

Download the installer for your operating system.

Open the downloaded installer.

Follow the installation instructions.

Select Android SDK and other required components.

Complete the installation.

Open Android Studio and create a new project.

After installation, developers can use the emulator to test applications. A stable internet connection is helpful during setup.

q: Q11. Classify the types of applications that can be developed using Android.
a:
Android supports different types of mobile applications.

Native Apps: Developed specifically for Android using Java or Kotlin.
Web Apps: Applications accessed through a mobile web browser.
Hybrid Apps: Combine web technologies and native features.
Gaming Apps: Used for entertainment and playing games.
Business Apps: Used for banking, shopping and office work.

Android also supports educational, healthcare and social media applications. These apps make daily activities easier and faster.

q: Q12. Distinguish between Android and other mobile operating systems.
a:
Android and other mobile operating systems have different features.

Android: Developed by Google and based on Linux.
iOS: Developed by Apple for Apple devices.
Customization: Android offers more customization options.
Devices: Android runs on devices from many companies, while iOS runs on Apple devices.
Applications: Both support large application stores.

Android is more flexible, while iOS provides a controlled ecosystem. Both offer security and user-friendly features.

q: Q13. Compare Android Studio with Eclipse for Android development.
a:
Android Studio and Eclipse are development tools used for programming.

Android Studio: Official IDE for Android development.
Eclipse: General-purpose IDE that previously supported Android development.
Interface: Android Studio provides modern development tools.
Features: Android Studio includes a layout editor, emulator and Gradle support.
Support: Android Studio receives official Android development support.

Android Studio is better for modern Android applications, while Eclipse is an older development environment.

q: Q14. Illustrate the basic structure of an Android project.
a:
An Android project contains different files and folders required to develop an application.

Manifest: Contains application information and permissions.
Java/Kotlin: Contains the application source code.
Res Folder: Stores images, layouts and strings.
Gradle Scripts: Manage dependencies and project building.
Assets: Stores additional files used by the application.

These components work together to create an Android application. Android Studio organizes them properly for easy development and management.

q: Q15. Apply the steps to create and run a simple Android app.
a:
The following steps are used to create and run a simple Android application.

Open Android Studio.

Click on New Project.

Select Empty Activity.

Enter the application name.

Choose Java or Kotlin.

Write the application code.

Design the user interface.

Click the Run button.

Select an emulator or connected Android device.

The application will start running. Developers can test its features and correct errors.

q: Q16. Demonstrate how to enable developer options on an Android device.
a:
Developer Options is a special Android setting used for testing and debugging applications.

Follow these steps:

Open the Settings app.

Select About Phone.

Find the Build Number option.

Tap Build Number seven times.

Enter your phone password if required.

A message will show that Developer Options is enabled.

Return to Settings and open Developer Options.

It provides features like USB debugging, animation control and performance testing.

q: Q17. Recognize the importance of the Google Play Store in Android development.
a:
Google Play Store is the official application store for most Android devices. It plays an important role in Android development.

It allows developers to publish applications.

Users can download and install apps.

It provides application updates.

It checks applications for security threats.

It helps developers reach millions of users.

Developers can also manage app releases and monitor downloads through Google Play Console. It connects developers with Android users worldwide.

q: Q18. Describe the purpose of Android intents.
a:
An Intent is a messaging object used to communicate between Android components. It helps one activity start another activity or perform an action.

Its main purposes are:

Open another activity.

Start a background service.

Share data between components.

Open a web page or dialer.

Send information to another application.

There are two main types: Explicit Intent and Implicit Intent. Intents make communication between Android applications easier and more flexible.

q: Q19. Explain the use of the AndroidManifest.xml file in an app.
a:
AndroidManifest.xml is an important configuration file in every Android application. It provides essential information about the application to the Android system.

Its main uses are:

Defines the application name.

Declares activities and services.

Specifies required permissions.

Defines application icons and themes.

Declares supported features.

For example, an application needs camera permission to use the device camera. The Android system reads this file before running the application.

q: Q20. Summarize how text-to-speech is used in mobile applications.
a:
Text-to-Speech (TTS) is a technology that converts written text into spoken words. Android provides a TextToSpeech class for this purpose.

Its main uses are:

Reading text aloud.

Helping visually impaired users.

Providing voice instructions.

Supporting language learning.

Improving user accessibility.

For example, a navigation app can speak directions like "Turn left". Developers can use the Android TextToSpeech API to add this feature to their applications.

q: Q21. Classify the types of user interfaces found in Android apps.
a:
Android applications use different types of user interfaces to interact with users.

Text Interface: Uses TextView to display information.
Input Interface: Uses EditText to accept user input.
Button Interface: Uses buttons to perform actions.
Selection Interface: Uses CheckBox, RadioButton and Spinner.
Image Interface: Uses ImageView to display pictures.

These UI components help users interact with applications easily. A good interface makes an application attractive and user-friendly.

q: Q22. Distinguish between a service and an activity in Android.
a:
Activity and Service are important components of Android applications.

Activity: Represents a screen that users can see and interact with.
Service: Performs operations in the background.
Activity: Requires user interaction.
Service: Can work without a visible user interface.
Example: A login screen uses an Activity, while music playback can use a Service.

Both components help Android applications perform different tasks efficiently.

q: Q23. Explain the role of Toast messages in debugging Android apps.
a:
A Toast is a small message displayed on the Android screen for a short time. It provides simple information to users and developers.

Its main uses are:

Shows success messages.

Displays error information.

Confirms user actions.

Helps check whether an operation works.

Provides temporary notifications.

For example, after successful login, an app can display "Login Successful". Toast messages are simple and disappear automatically without disturbing the user.

q: Q24. Summarize the benefits of using Logcat in Android development.
a:
Logcat is a debugging tool available in Android Studio. It displays messages generated by Android applications and the Android system.

Its main benefits are:

Helps identify application errors.

Displays warning messages.

Shows debugging information.

Helps developers track application activities.

Makes troubleshooting easier.

Developers can use different log levels such as Debug, Info, Warning and Error. Logcat helps find problems and improve application performance.

q: Q25. Explain the difference between Button and ImageButton in Android UI.
a:
Button and ImageButton are Android UI components used to perform actions.

Button: Displays text to represent an action.
ImageButton: Displays an image instead of text.
Button: Used for actions like Submit and Login.
ImageButton: Used for icons like Search and Camera.
Appearance: Button mainly shows text, while ImageButton displays graphical content.

Both components respond to user clicks. They make Android applications easier to use and understand.

q: Q26. Illustrate adding EditText and Button to a LinearLayout using XML.
a:
LinearLayout arranges UI components vertically or horizontally. EditText accepts user input, while Button performs an action.

The following XML creates a simple login interface:

<LinearLayout

android: layout_width="match_parent"
android: layout_height="wrap_content"
android: orientation="vertical">

<EditText

android: layout_width="match_parent"
android: layout_height="wrap_content"
android: hint="Enter Name"/>

<Button

android: layout_width="wrap_content"
android: layout_height="wrap_content"
android: text="Submit"/>
</LinearLayout>

This layout displays an input field and a Submit button vertically.

q: Q27. Construct a UI layout with CheckBox and ProgressBar.
a:
CheckBox allows users to select or deselect an option. ProgressBar displays the progress of an operation.

The following XML creates a simple interface:

<LinearLayout

android: layout_width="match_parent"
android: layout_height="wrap_content"
android: orientation="vertical">

<CheckBox

android: layout_width="wrap_content"
android: layout_height="wrap_content"
android: text="Accept Terms"/>

<ProgressBar

android: layout_width="wrap_content"
android: layout_height="wrap_content"
style="?android: attr/progressBarStyleHorizontal"
android: progress="50"/>
</LinearLayout>

This layout displays a checkbox and a progress bar.

q: Q28. Develop a scenario using ToggleButton to control a setting.
a:
ToggleButton is an Android UI component used to switch a setting between two states, ON and OFF.

For example, it can control Wi-Fi in an application.

The following XML creates a ToggleButton:

<ToggleButton

android: id="@+id/toggle"
android: layout_width="wrap_content"
android: layout_height="wrap_content"
android: textOn="ON"
android: textOff="OFF"/>

When the user clicks the button, its state changes. Developers can use this state to control application settings such as notifications or sound.

q: Q29. Explain the use of AlertDialog for user decisions.
a:
AlertDialog is a pop-up window used to display important messages and collect user decisions. It helps applications communicate with users.

Its main uses are:

Shows warning messages.

Asks for user confirmation.

Displays important information.

Provides Yes and No options.

Prevents accidental actions.

For example, before deleting a file, an application can display "Are you sure?" with Yes and No buttons. It makes applications safer and more user-friendly.

q: Q30. Illustrate the difference between SeekBar and RatingBar in Android.
a:
SeekBar and RatingBar are Android UI components used for different purposes.

SeekBar: Allows users to select a value by moving a slider.
RatingBar: Allows users to give ratings using stars.
SeekBar: Used for controlling volume or brightness.
RatingBar: Used for rating products or services.
Appearance: SeekBar looks like a sliding bar, while RatingBar displays stars.

Both components help users provide input easily through the application interface.

q: Q31. Construct the usage of AutoCompleteTextView for user input.
a:
AutoCompleteTextView is an Android UI component that suggests words automatically when users start typing. It helps users enter information quickly and correctly.

Its main uses are:

Provides automatic suggestions.

Reduces typing effort.

Saves users' time.

Reduces spelling mistakes.

Improves user experience.

For example, a search application can suggest city names when users type the first few letters. Developers can use an ArrayAdapter to provide suggestions to AutoCompleteTextView.

q: Q32. Analyze the causes of UI lag during complex graphics rendering in Android apps.
a:
UI lag happens when an Android application takes too much time to display graphics or respond to user actions.

The main causes are:
Heavy Graphics: Complex images require more processing.
Slow CPU: The processor cannot complete tasks quickly.
Memory Usage: High memory consumption reduces performance.
Poor Coding: Unnecessary operations make the app slow.
Overdraw: Drawing the same area multiple times wastes resources.

Developers can improve performance by optimizing images, layouts and code.

q: Q33. Evaluate the effectiveness of GPU overdraw analysis for UI performance optimization.
a:
GPU overdraw analysis is a tool used to identify areas where Android draws the same screen multiple times. It helps developers improve application performance.

Its benefits are:

Identifies unnecessary drawing.

Reduces GPU workload.

Improves screen rendering speed.

Saves battery power.

Makes animations smoother.

Developers can enable Debug GPU Overdraw from Developer Options. It uses different colours to show overdraw areas. Removing unnecessary backgrounds and UI layers helps improve performance.

q: Q34. Evaluate how loading large bitmap images affects the memory usage of a mobile app.
a:
Large bitmap images consume more memory in Android applications. Loading too many large images can make an application slow or unstable.

Its effects are:

Increases RAM usage.

Makes the application slower.

Can cause OutOfMemoryError.

Reduces overall performance.

May cause application crashes.

Developers should resize and compress images before loading them. Using suitable image formats and image-loading libraries helps reduce memory usage and improves application performance.

q: Q35. Evaluate the benefits of using asynchronous loading for multimedia assets.
a:
Asynchronous loading means loading images, videos and other files in the background without stopping the main UI thread.

Its benefits are:

Keeps the application responsive.

Prevents UI freezing.

Improves loading speed.

Provides a better user experience.

Allows multiple tasks to work efficiently.

For example, an application can load images from the internet while users continue scrolling. Developers can use background threads and image-loading libraries for this purpose.

q: Q36. Analyze the role of multithreading in improving graphics performance.
a:
Multithreading is a technique that allows an application to perform multiple tasks at the same time using different threads. It helps improve Android application performance.

Its main roles are:

Loads images in background threads.

Reduces work on the main thread.

Prevents screen freezing.

Improves application responsiveness.

Supports smooth user interactions.

For example, an app can download images while displaying other content. Developers must manage threads properly to avoid memory and synchronization problems.

q: Q37. Evaluate strategies for optimizing graphics for different device resolutions.
a:
Android devices have different screen sizes and resolutions. Graphics optimization helps applications look clear on all devices.

The main strategies are:
Responsive Design: Adjust layouts according to screen size.
Density-independent Pixels: Use dp for layout measurements.
Scalable Images: Use suitable image resources.
Vector Drawables: Use graphics that scale without losing quality.
Image Compression: Reduce image size.

These strategies improve application appearance, reduce memory usage and provide a better user experience.

q: Q38. Analyze the challenges of implementing peer-to-peer architecture in mobile field service apps.
a:
Peer-to-peer (P2P) architecture allows mobile devices to communicate directly without always using a central server. Implementing it in field service applications creates some challenges.

Connectivity: Devices may lose network connections.
Security: Data must be protected during communication.
Synchronization: Devices must share updated information.
Battery Usage: Continuous communication consumes battery.
Device Compatibility: Different devices may have different capabilities.

Proper encryption, synchronization and connection management help solve these problems.

q: Q39. Justify the effect of using multiple UI layers like LinearLayout, RelativeLayout, and ConstraintLayout on app performance.
a:
Android layouts arrange UI components on the screen. Using too many nested layouts can reduce application performance.

LinearLayout: Arranges components vertically or horizontally.
RelativeLayout: Positions components relative to other views.
ConstraintLayout: Creates flexible layouts with fewer nested views.
Deep Nesting: Increases layout calculation time.
Optimization: Reducing unnecessary layers improves rendering speed.

ConstraintLayout is useful for creating complex interfaces with a flatter layout structure. It helps improve performance.

q: Q40. Analyze the importance of memory management in Android multimedia apps.
a:
Memory management is important in Android multimedia applications because images, videos and audio files consume large amounts of memory.

Its importance includes:

Prevents application crashes.

Reduces unnecessary memory usage.

Improves application speed.

Helps manage large media files.

Provides smooth multimedia playback.

Developers should release unused resources, resize images and avoid memory leaks. Proper memory management makes applications stable, efficient and user-friendly.

q: Q41. Evaluate the effectiveness of asset packaging and deployment strategies for Android field service apps.
a:
Asset packaging means including images, icons, fonts and other resources inside an Android application. Proper packaging makes field service apps easier to use.

Its benefits are:

Keeps required resources organized.

Reduces unnecessary file downloads.

Supports offline access.

Improves application performance.

Makes deployment easier.

Developers can use APK or Android App Bundle (AAB) for distribution. They should compress assets and test the application before publishing it.

q: Q42. Compare static code analysis and dynamic testing for identifying security vulnerabilities in Android apps.
a:
Static code analysis and dynamic testing are two methods used to find security problems in Android applications.

Static Analysis: Checks source code without running the application.
Dynamic Testing: Checks the application while it is running.
Static Analysis: Finds coding mistakes and insecure functions.
Dynamic Testing: Finds runtime security problems.
Purpose: Both help improve application security.

Using both methods together provides better protection and helps developers identify more vulnerabilities.

q: Q43. Distinguish between authentication and authorization in mobile app security.
a:
Authentication and authorization are important security processes in mobile applications.

Authentication: Checks the identity of a user.
Authorization: Checks what the user is allowed to access.
Authentication: Uses passwords, OTP or biometrics.
Authorization: Uses roles and permissions.
Example: Login verifies a user, while admin access allows only authorized users to manage data.

Both processes protect applications from unauthorized access and keep user information safe.

q: Q44. Compare storing sensitive data in internal storage versus external storage on Android devices.
a:
Android provides internal and external storage for saving application data.

Internal Storage: Stores data in the application's private area.
External Storage: Stores files in shared or external storage areas.
Security: Internal storage provides better privacy by default.
Access: External storage may be accessible to other applications, depending on permissions and storage rules.
Usage: Internal storage is suitable for sensitive information, while external storage is useful for shared files.

Sensitive data should always be encrypted.

q: Q45. Evaluate the effectiveness of using HTTPS over HTTP for data transmission in mobile apps.
a:
HTTPS is more secure than HTTP because it uses encryption to protect data during communication.

Its benefits are:
Encryption: Protects transmitted information.
Authentication: Helps verify the server's identity.
Data Protection: Prevents unauthorized reading.
Integrity: Helps detect data modification.
Privacy: Protects passwords and personal information.

HTTP sends data without transport encryption. Therefore, Android applications should use HTTPS for secure communication with backend servers.

q: Q46. Distinguish between user-granted permissions and application-defined permissions in Android security.
a:
Android uses different permissions to control access to application features and resources.

User-granted Permissions: Allow users to approve access to sensitive features.
Application-defined Permissions: Created by developers to protect their application's components.
Examples: Camera and location permissions require user approval.
Purpose: Application-defined permissions control access between applications.
Security: Both help prevent unauthorized access.

These permissions protect user information and improve Android application security.

q: Q47. Compare the impact of regular dependency updates versus outdated libraries on app security.
a:
Dependencies are external libraries used in Android application development. Keeping them updated is important for security.

Regular Updates: Fix known security vulnerabilities.
Outdated Libraries: May contain security weaknesses.
Performance: Updated libraries may improve application performance.
Compatibility: Updates support newer Android versions.
Risk: Old dependencies can allow attackers to exploit applications.

Developers should regularly check, update and test dependencies to keep applications secure and reliable.

q: Q48. Justify the need for security in mobile app development.
a:
Security is necessary in mobile application development because apps store and process important user information.

Its main importance is:

Protects personal information.

Prevents unauthorized access.

Protects passwords and financial data.

Prevents malware and cyberattacks.

Builds user trust.

Developers should use encryption, authentication, secure communication and proper permissions. Good security practices make mobile applications safer, more reliable and trustworthy for users.

q: Q49. Compare secure communication protocols such as HTTPS with insecure protocols for backend integration.
a:
Communication protocols help mobile applications exchange data with backend servers.

HTTPS: Uses encryption to protect transmitted data.
HTTP: Does not provide transport encryption.
Security: HTTPS protects sensitive information.
Authentication: HTTPS helps verify the server using digital certificates.
Usage: HTTPS is suitable for login, payment and personal data.

Insecure protocols can expose information to attackers. Therefore, developers should use HTTPS for secure backend communication.

q: Q50. Distinguish between input validation and output encoding as security measures.
a:
Input validation and output encoding are important security techniques used in mobile applications.

Input Validation: Checks whether user input is correct and acceptable.
Output Encoding: Converts special characters into a safe format before displaying output.
Purpose: Validation rejects invalid data.
Purpose: Encoding helps prevent harmful code execution.
Example: Checking an email format is validation, while encoding HTML characters is output encoding.

Both techniques help protect applications from security attacks.

q: Q51. Evaluate the importance of early security planning in the mobile app development process.
a:
Early security planning means considering security from the beginning of application development. It helps developers build safer applications.

Its importance includes:

Identifies security risks early.

Protects user information.

Reduces future development costs.

Prevents common security problems.

Improves application reliability.

Developers should plan authentication, authorization, encryption and secure data storage before coding. Early security planning reduces vulnerabilities and makes applications more trustworthy.

q: Q52. Define Android architecture and explain its main layers.
a:
Android architecture is the structure of the Android operating system. It consists of different layers that work together to run applications smoothly. It helps developers create and manage mobile applications.

The main layers are:
Linux Kernel: It is the bottom layer. It manages memory, security, hardware and device drivers.
Hardware Abstraction Layer (HAL): It connects hardware components with the Android software.
Android Runtime (ART): It provides the environment for running Android applications.
Native Libraries: These libraries support graphics, databases and multimedia.
Application Framework: It provides services like activity management, notifications and location services.
Applications: This is the top layer. It contains built-in and user-installed applications.

All layers work together to provide a smooth user experience. Android architecture makes application development easier, flexible and organized.

q: Q54. Describe the role of frameworks and tools in mobile app development.
a:
Frameworks and tools play an important role in mobile application development. They provide ready-made features and resources that help developers create applications easily and quickly.

Their main roles are:
Frameworks: Provide reusable code and libraries for application development.
Development Tools: Help developers write, test and manage code.
Debugging Tools: Help identify and correct programming errors.
Testing Tools: Check application performance and functionality.
Design Tools: Help create attractive user interfaces.

For example, Android Studio is used for Android development, while Flutter is used to develop applications for multiple platforms. React Native is another popular framework.

These frameworks and tools reduce development time, improve code quality and make application maintenance easier. They also help developers create applications for different devices.

q: Q55. Distinguish emulator testing from real device testing in Android development.
a:
Emulator testing and real device testing are two methods used to test Android applications.

Emulator Testing: Runs applications on a virtual Android device using a computer.
Real Device Testing: Runs applications on an actual smartphone or tablet.
Cost: Emulator testing does not require purchasing multiple devices.
Performance: Real devices provide more accurate performance results.
Hardware: Real device testing checks actual GPS, camera, sensors and battery usage.

Emulators are useful during the early development process because they allow testing on different screen sizes and Android versions. However, they cannot completely reproduce real-world conditions.

Real device testing is important before publishing an application. Both methods should be used to ensure better application quality and performance.

q: Q56. Illustrate the process to create and run a "Hello World" app in Android Studio.
a:
A Hello World application is a simple Android application that displays the message "Hello World" on the screen. It helps beginners understand basic Android development.

The following steps are used:

Open Android Studio on your computer.

Click on New Project.

Select Empty Activity.

Enter the project name as HelloWorld.

Select Java or Kotlin as the programming language, depending on the project template.

Click Finish to create the project.

Open the main activity and design the screen.

Add a TextView with the text "Hello World".

Start an Android Emulator or connect a real device.

Click the Run button.

The application will open and display Hello World. This process teaches beginners how to create, build and run Android applications.

q: Q57. Apply mobile software engineering concepts to handle device diversity in Android.
a:
Device diversity means Android applications run on different devices with different screen sizes, hardware and operating system versions. Mobile software engineering helps developers handle these differences.

The main concepts are:
Responsive Design: Creates layouts that adjust to different screen sizes.
Resource Management: Uses different images and layouts for different screen densities.
Compatibility Testing: Tests applications on different Android versions.
Modular Development: Divides applications into smaller reusable components.
Performance Optimization: Reduces memory and battery consumption.

Developers should use dp for layout measurements and scalable images for better display. They should also test applications on emulators and real devices.

These techniques make Android applications compatible, reliable and user-friendly across different devices.

q: Q53. Explain the use of basic views like TextView and EditText.
a:
TextView and EditText are basic UI components used in Android applications. They help users read information and enter data.

TextView: It is used to display text on the screen.
EditText: It allows users to enter and edit information.
TextView Example: Displays messages like "Welcome to Android".
EditText Example: Accepts a user's name, email or password.
User Interaction: EditText collects information, while TextView presents information.
Example XML:

<TextView

android: layout_width="wrap_content"
android: layout_height="wrap_content"
android: text="Enter Your Name"/>

<EditText

android: layout_width="match_parent"
android: layout_height="wrap_content"
android: hint="Your Name"/>

Both components are important for designing simple and user-friendly interfaces. They are commonly used in login forms, registration pages and other Android applications.

q: Q58. Explain how to design a UI using LinearLayout.
a:
LinearLayout is an Android layout that arranges UI components in a single direction. It can arrange components vertically or horizontally.

The main steps are:

Open the Android Studio project.

Open the XML layout file.

Add a LinearLayout element.

Set its width and height.

Set the orientation as vertical or horizontal.

Add UI components like TextView, EditText and Button.

Set suitable margins and padding.

Run the application to check the design.

Example:

<LinearLayout

android: layout_width="match_parent"
android: layout_height="wrap_content"
android: orientation="vertical">

<TextView

android: layout_width="wrap_content"
android: layout_height="wrap_content"
android: text="Welcome"/>

<Button

android: layout_width="wrap_content"
android: layout_height="wrap_content"
android: text="Submit"/>
</LinearLayout>

LinearLayout makes UI design simple and organized.

q: Q59. Describe steps to add a Button with an event handler.
a:
A Button is an Android UI component used to perform an action when the user clicks it. An event handler defines what happens after clicking the button.

The main steps are:

Open the Android Studio project.

Add a Button in the XML layout.

Give the button an ID.

Open the activity source code.

Find the button using its ID.

Set an OnClickListener.

Write the required action inside the listener.

Run the application and test the button.

Example in Java: 
Button btn = findViewById(R.id.button);
btn.setOnClickListener(v -> {
Toast.makeText(this,

"Button Clicked",

Toast.LENGTH_SHORT).show();

});

When the user clicks the button, a Toast message appears. Event handlers make Android applications interactive and useful.

q: Q60. Compare LinearLayout and RelativeLayout for designing Android UIs.
a:
LinearLayout and RelativeLayout are Android layout types used to arrange UI components. They have different working methods.

LinearLayout: Arranges components vertically or horizontally.
RelativeLayout: Positions components relative to other views or the parent layout.
Simplicity: LinearLayout is easier for simple screen designs.
Flexibility: RelativeLayout provides more flexible positioning.
Nesting: Complex LinearLayouts may require multiple nested layouts, while RelativeLayout can reduce some nesting.

For example, LinearLayout is useful for a simple login form. RelativeLayout can be useful when placing a button below a text field.

Both layouts help create Android interfaces. Developers should choose the layout according to the design requirements. ConstraintLayout is another modern option for creating complex interfaces.

q: Q61. Evaluate the effectiveness of using intents for communication between Android components.
a:
Intents are messaging objects used to communicate between different Android components. They help activities, services and applications perform actions.

Their benefits are:
Activity Communication: Intents can open another activity.
Service Communication: They can start or interact with services.
Data Sharing: They can carry information between components.
Application Integration: They can open external applications.
Flexibility: They support explicit and implicit communication.

For example, an application can use an implicit intent to open a website in a browser. An explicit intent can open a particular activity within the same application.

However, developers must handle sensitive information carefully and validate incoming data. Intents make Android applications flexible, organized and easier to connect with other applications.

q: Q78. Compare the use of Jetpack Compose and XML layouts for Android UI development.
a:
Jetpack Compose and XML layouts are two methods of designing Android user interfaces.

Jetpack Compose: A modern UI toolkit that uses Kotlin code to create interfaces.
XML Layouts: Use XML files to describe screen designs.
Code: Compose uses Kotlin, while XML layouts separate design from activity code.
Updates: Compose automatically updates the UI when application state changes.
Learning: XML is familiar to traditional Android developers, while Compose requires understanding declarative programming.

Jetpack Compose reduces the need for separate XML layout files and makes UI development more modern. XML layouts are still useful in existing Android projects.

Both methods can create attractive and interactive applications. The choice depends on project requirements and developer experience.

q: Q81. Justify using button controls in mobile apps.
a:
Button controls are important UI components in mobile applications. They allow users to perform different actions by simply touching the screen.

Their main advantages are:
Easy Interaction: Users can perform actions easily.
Navigation: Buttons help users move between screens.
Form Submission: They submit login and registration details.
User Feedback: They can display messages after an action.
Accessibility: Properly designed buttons support easier interaction.

For example, a shopping application uses buttons like Add to Cart, Buy Now and Checkout.

Buttons make applications interactive and user-friendly. Developers should use clear text, suitable sizes and proper spacing. They should also provide accessible labels and visible feedback after clicks.

q: Q82. Justify using toggle buttons for user interaction in Android apps.
a:
A ToggleButton is an Android UI component that allows users to switch between two states, usually ON and OFF. It is useful for controlling application settings.

Its main advantages are:
Easy Control: Users can change settings with one click.
Two States: It supports ON and OFF conditions.
Quick Interaction: It reduces the number of steps.
Visual Feedback: It displays the current state.
Practical Usage: It can control sound, notifications and other application settings.

For example, a music application can use a toggle button to enable or disable repeat mode.

Toggle buttons make applications easier to use. Developers should provide clear labels and accessible descriptions so that users understand the current setting.

q: Q87. Develop a user interface model using menus, dialogs, and notifications to enhance usability.
a:
Menus, dialogs and notifications are important Android UI components. They help users access features, make decisions and receive important information.

A simple interface model can be designed as follows:

Menus: Provide options like Home, Settings, Profile and Logout.
Dialogs: Display confirmation messages before important actions.
Notifications: Inform users about background activities and updates.
User Interaction: Allow users to select options and respond to messages.
Feedback: Provide clear information after completing an action.

For example, a shopping application can use a menu for navigation, an AlertDialog before deleting an order and a notification when the order is delivered.

These components improve communication between the application and users. Properly designed menus, dialogs and notifications make applications organized and user-friendly.

q: Q89. Express the advantages of using RecyclerView for dynamic data display in Android.
a:
RecyclerView is an Android UI component used to display large lists of data efficiently. It reuses existing item views instead of creating new views for every item.

Its main advantages are:
Memory Efficiency: Reuses item views and reduces unnecessary memory usage.
Better Performance: Displays large amounts of data smoothly.
Flexible Layouts: Supports lists, grids and other arrangements.
Customization: Developers can design different item layouts.
Animations: Supports item animations and changes.

For example, a shopping application can use RecyclerView to display hundreds of products with images and prices.

RecyclerView uses an Adapter and ViewHolder to manage data and views. It is useful for applications that display changing or large amounts of information.

q: Q91. Compare the use of toggle buttons and custom controls for improving accessibility.
a:
Toggle buttons and custom controls are used to improve user interaction in Android applications. Both can be designed to support accessibility.

ToggleButton: Provides a simple ON/OFF control.
Custom Controls: Allow developers to create special controls according to application needs.
Ease of Use: Toggle buttons are simple and familiar.
Flexibility: Custom controls provide more design and functionality options.
Accessibility: Both should provide clear labels, descriptions and proper touch areas.

For example, a toggle button can enable notifications, while a custom control can adjust text size.

Toggle buttons are suitable for simple settings. Custom controls are useful for special requirements. Developers should support screen readers and provide clear feedback to all users.

q: Q62. Explain the use of multimedia in Android applications.
a:
Multimedia means using different types of media, such as images, audio, video and animation, in an application. Android supports multimedia features to make applications more attractive and interactive.

Its main uses are:
Images: Display photographs, icons and graphics.
Audio: Play music, voice messages and sound effects.
Video: Play educational videos and movies.
Animation: Create moving objects and visual effects.
Camera: Capture photographs and record videos.

For example, a learning application can display images, play recorded lessons and show educational videos.

Android provides multimedia tools and APIs to manage these features. Multimedia improves communication, user engagement and the overall experience of mobile applications.

q: Q63. Evaluate the benefits and challenges of using OpenGL ES for graphics rendering in Android apps.
a:
OpenGL ES is a graphics programming interface used to create 2D and 3D graphics in Android applications. It uses the GPU to render complex graphics.

Its benefits are:
High Performance: Uses GPU processing for graphics.
3D Graphics: Supports three-dimensional objects and animations.
Gaming: Useful for developing mobile games.
Visual Effects: Creates attractive graphics and animations.
Hardware Support: Uses supported graphics hardware.

However, it also has some challenges. It requires programming knowledge, can be difficult to learn and may have compatibility issues across devices.

For example, developers can use OpenGL ES to create a 3D racing game. It is useful when an application requires advanced graphics and smooth rendering.

q: Q64. Analyze the impact of packaging multimedia content on Android app deployment and performance.
a:
Multimedia packaging means including images, audio, videos and other media files inside an Android application or delivering them separately.

Its main impacts are:
Application Size: Large media files increase the app size.
Loading Speed: Properly compressed assets load faster.
Memory Usage: Large images and videos consume more memory.
Offline Access: Packaged content can be available without internet access.
Deployment: Proper asset organization makes application distribution easier.

For example, a learning application can include small images and audio lessons inside its package. Large videos can be downloaded when required.

Developers should compress multimedia files and remove unused assets. Android App Bundle and suitable resource management techniques help improve application delivery and performance.

q: Q65. Evaluate the effectiveness of location-based services in enhancing field service applications.
a:
Location-based services use GPS and other location technologies to identify the geographical position of a mobile device. They are very useful in field service applications.

Their benefits are:
Live Tracking: Managers can track field employees.
Navigation: Workers can find the correct customer location.
Attendance: Employees can mark attendance using GPS.
Route Planning: Helps find suitable travel routes.
Time Saving: Reduces unnecessary travelling.

For example, a delivery company can use location-based services to track delivery staff and check their current location.

However, GPS may not work accurately indoors and can consume battery power. Location access also requires user permission. Proper implementation improves productivity, communication and field management.

q: Q66. Analyze the advantages and limitations of peer-to-peer architecture in mobile agent communication.
a:
Peer-to-peer (P2P) architecture is a communication model where devices communicate directly with each other without always depending on a central server. Mobile agents can use this architecture to exchange information.

Its advantages are:
Direct Communication: Devices can share data directly.
Reduced Server Load: Reduces dependence on a central server.
Resource Sharing: Devices can share files and information.
Flexibility: Supports communication between different devices.
Scalability: Can support distributed communication.

However, it has limitations such as security risks, network problems, battery consumption and data synchronization difficulties.

For example, field workers can share task information directly when network conditions are suitable. Proper encryption and connection management are necessary for secure communication.

q: Q79. Evaluate the impact of background threads on performance and user experience in Android apps.
a:
Background threads are used to perform tasks without blocking the main UI thread. They help Android applications remain responsive while processing data.

Their main benefits are:
Smooth Interface: Prevents the screen from freezing.
Data Loading: Loads information from servers in the background.
File Processing: Handles large files without blocking user interaction.
Better Performance: Separates heavy tasks from UI operations.
Improved Experience: Allows users to continue using the application.

For example, a shopping application can download product images while users scroll through the product list.

However, too many background threads may consume memory and battery. Developers should use suitable tools such as ExecutorService, Kotlin coroutines or WorkManager according to the task.

q: Q97. Compare single-threading and multithreading in Android apps.
a:
Single-threading and multithreading are two methods of executing tasks in Android applications.

Single-threading: Executes tasks using one thread.
Multithreading: Executes multiple tasks using different threads.
Performance: Multithreading can improve task handling.
UI: Heavy operations on the main thread can freeze the interface.
Complexity: Multithreading requires proper thread management.

For example, a simple calculator can work with a single main thread, while a multimedia application may use multiple threads for downloading and processing files.

Single-threading is simple but may become slow during heavy operations. Multithreading improves responsiveness but requires careful synchronization and resource management.

q: Q98. Evaluate why good graphics and UI performance are important in Android apps.
a:
Good graphics and UI performance are important because they make Android applications attractive, smooth and easy to use.

Their importance includes:
User Experience: Provides a comfortable application experience.
Fast Response: Allows users to perform actions quickly.
Smooth Animation: Makes screen transitions and animations better.
User Engagement: Attractive designs encourage users to use the application.
Battery Efficiency: Optimized graphics can reduce unnecessary resource usage.

For example, a shopping application with clear product images and smooth scrolling is easier to use.

Poor graphics and slow interfaces may frustrate users and cause them to uninstall the application. Developers should optimize images, layouts and animations to improve performance.

q: Q99. Distinguish between Android Canvas and OpenGL for drawing graphics.
a:
Android Canvas and OpenGL are two technologies used for drawing graphics in Android applications.

Canvas: A 2D drawing API used to draw shapes, text and images.
OpenGL: A graphics API used for advanced 2D and 3D rendering.
Complexity: Canvas is easier to learn and use.
Performance: OpenGL uses GPU acceleration for supported graphics operations.
Applications: Canvas is useful for simple drawing, while OpenGL is suitable for games and complex graphics.

For example, Canvas can draw a simple circle or line. OpenGL can create a rotating 3D object.

Both technologies are useful. Developers should choose according to the graphics requirements of the application.

q: Q100. Compare location-based services and mobility features in Android.
a:
Location-based services and mobility features are important in Android applications. They help users access information and services while moving.

Location-Based Services: Use GPS, Wi-Fi or mobile networks to identify a device's location.
Mobility Features: Support mobile activities such as movement, connectivity and portable access.
Purpose: Location services provide geographical information.
Purpose: Mobility features help applications work across different environments.
Examples: Google Maps uses location services, while mobile notifications support users on the move.

Location-based services are useful for navigation, tracking and attendance. Mobility features support communication and application access from different places.

Both improve the usefulness of Android applications. Developers should consider battery usage, connectivity and privacy.

q: Q101. Evaluate the use of peer-to-peer architecture and mobile agents in Android.
a:
Peer-to-peer architecture and mobile agents are useful concepts in distributed mobile applications. They help devices communicate and exchange information.

Their uses are:
Peer-to-Peer: Allows devices to communicate directly.
Mobile Agents: Software programs that perform tasks on behalf of users.
Data Sharing: Helps exchange information between devices.
Reduced Server Dependency: Some tasks can be performed without a central server.
Automation: Mobile agents can perform selected tasks automatically.

For example, field workers can exchange task information using peer-to-peer communication. A mobile agent can collect and process task details.

However, these technologies may face security, connectivity and synchronization problems. Encryption and proper access control are important for safe communication.

q: Q67. Analyze risks of storing sensitive data on external storage in Android.
a:
External storage is used to store files such as images, videos and documents. Storing sensitive information in external storage can create security risks.

The main risks are:
Unauthorized Access: Other applications may access shared files, depending on permissions and storage rules.
Data Theft: Personal information may be copied by unauthorized users.
Data Modification: Files may be changed or deleted.
Privacy Problems: Sensitive information may become exposed.
Device Loss: Data may be accessed if storage is not properly protected.

For example, storing passwords or banking details in unprotected external storage is unsafe.

Developers should use private internal storage for sensitive information and apply encryption where necessary. Proper access control improves application security.

q: Q68. Evaluate the impact of biometric authentication in financial apps.
a:
Biometric authentication uses physical characteristics such as fingerprints or facial recognition to verify a user's identity. It is useful in financial applications.

Its benefits are:
Better Security: Makes unauthorized access more difficult.
Easy Login: Users do not need to enter passwords every time.
Fast Verification: Authentication takes very little time.
User Convenience: Provides an easy login experience.
Fraud Prevention: Adds another layer of identity verification.

For example, a banking application can use fingerprint authentication before allowing users to access their accounts.

However, biometric authentication has limitations. Sensor problems and device compatibility may affect it. Financial applications should also provide secure backup authentication and protect sensitive information.

q: Q69. Analyze consequences of not minimizing app permissions.
a:
Android permissions allow applications to access device features such as the camera, microphone, location and contacts. Requesting unnecessary permissions can create security problems.

The main consequences are:
Privacy Risks: Unnecessary access may expose personal information.
Security Problems: Attackers may misuse excessive permissions.
User Distrust: Users may feel unsafe.
Data Misuse: Applications may collect unnecessary information.
Compliance Issues: Excessive data collection may violate privacy requirements.

For example, a calculator application does not normally need access to contacts or location.

Developers should follow the principle of least privilege. They should request only necessary permissions and explain their purpose clearly. This improves security and user trust.

q: Q70. Evaluate the effectiveness of regular security testing during development.
a:
Regular security testing means checking an application repeatedly during development to identify security weaknesses. It helps developers protect applications from attacks.

Its benefits are:
Early Detection: Finds security problems before deployment.
Data Protection: Protects user information.
Error Correction: Helps developers fix vulnerabilities.
Better Quality: Improves application reliability.
Reduced Risk: Reduces the possibility of security attacks.

Developers can use static code analysis, dynamic testing and dependency scanning. They should also test authentication, permissions and API communication.

For example, a banking application should regularly test its login and payment features. Continuous security testing makes applications safer and more reliable.

q: Q71. Analyze the role of secure API communication in active transactions.
a:
Secure API communication protects information exchanged between mobile applications and backend servers. It is especially important during financial transactions.

Its main roles are:
Encryption: Protects sensitive transaction information.
Authentication: Verifies users and servers.
Data Integrity: Helps prevent unauthorized data modification.
Authorization: Ensures users can perform only permitted actions.
Transaction Safety: Helps protect payment and account details.

For example, when a user transfers money through a banking app, secure API communication protects the transaction data.

Developers should use HTTPS, secure authentication tokens and proper server-side validation. Sensitive information should never be exposed through insecure communication. These practices improve transaction security.

q: Q72. Evaluate challenges in maintaining secure architecture with frequent updates and libraries.
a:
Maintaining a secure Android architecture becomes challenging when applications receive frequent updates and use many external libraries.

The main challenges are:
New Vulnerabilities: Updated software may introduce security problems.
Outdated Libraries: Old dependencies may contain known weaknesses.
Compatibility: Updates may cause problems with existing features.
Testing: Every major change requires proper testing.
Dependency Management: Developers must track external libraries.

For example, an application using an outdated networking library may become vulnerable to attacks.

Developers should regularly update dependencies, review security reports and test new versions before deployment. Proper version control and automated security checks help maintain a secure application.

q: Q73. Analyze the impact of improper input validation on transaction security.
a:
Input validation checks whether the information entered by users is correct and acceptable. Improper validation can create serious security problems in financial transactions.

Its effects are:
Invalid Data: Incorrect transaction details may be accepted.
SQL Injection: Attackers may insert harmful database commands.
Data Manipulation: Transaction information may be changed.
Unauthorized Actions: Malicious input may exploit application weaknesses.
Financial Loss: Incorrect or manipulated transactions may cause losses.

For example, a banking application must validate account numbers and transaction amounts.

Developers should validate input on both the client side and server side. They should also use parameterized database queries and proper error handling. Good validation improves transaction safety.

q: Q74. Evaluate Android Keystore versus hardcoded credentials for security.
a:
Android Keystore and hardcoded credentials are two methods related to storing sensitive security information.

Android Keystore: Provides a secure system for storing cryptographic keys.
Hardcoded Credentials: Store passwords or keys directly inside application code.
Security: Keystore offers better protection for cryptographic keys.
Exposure: Hardcoded credentials can be discovered by examining application files.
Usage: Keystore is useful for protecting encryption keys and authentication-related secrets.

For example, a banking application can use Android Keystore to protect a cryptographic key used for data encryption.

Hardcoding passwords and secret keys is unsafe. Developers should use secure storage mechanisms and avoid keeping sensitive credentials directly in source code.

q: Q75. Analyze the effect of excessive permission requests on user trust.
a:
Android applications request permissions to access device features and personal information. Asking for too many permissions can reduce user trust.

Its effects are:
Privacy Concerns: Users may worry about personal information.
Reduced Trust: Applications may appear unsafe.
Installation Problems: Users may refuse to install the app.
Permission Denial: Users may reject important permissions.
Poor Experience: Frequent permission messages can annoy users.

For example, a calculator application requesting camera and microphone permissions may look suspicious.

Developers should request only necessary permissions and explain why they are needed. Permissions should be requested when the related feature is used. This improves transparency and user confidence.

q: Q76. Evaluate the benefits and limits of automated security testing tools.
a:
Automated security testing tools are software programs that help identify security problems in applications automatically. They reduce manual testing effort.

Their benefits are:
Fast Testing: Check applications quickly.
Early Detection: Find common security weaknesses.
Time Saving: Reduce repetitive manual work.
Continuous Checking: Can run during development.
Consistency: Perform repeated checks in a similar way.

However, these tools also have limitations. They may produce false warnings and cannot identify every security problem. Some complex vulnerabilities require manual testing.

For example, static analysis tools can identify insecure coding patterns. Developers should combine automated tools with manual security reviews for better protection.

q: Q90. Express the importance of proper permission management for location-based services.
a:
Permission management is important for location-based Android applications because they access users' geographical information. Proper permission handling protects privacy and improves security.

Its importance includes:
Privacy Protection: Prevents unnecessary location collection.
User Control: Allows users to grant or deny access.
Data Security: Reduces the risk of location information misuse.
Transparency: Explains why location access is needed.
Battery Saving: Avoids unnecessary location tracking.

For example, a field attendance application should request location permission when an employee marks attendance.

Developers should request only necessary permissions and follow Android's permission rules. They should also protect stored location information and stop tracking when it is no longer required.

q: Q77. Compare SQLite and cloud storage solutions for managing user data in a mobile app.
a:
SQLite and cloud storage are two methods used to store and manage user data in Android applications.

SQLite: A local database that stores information directly on the mobile device.
Cloud Storage: Stores information on remote internet servers.
Internet: SQLite can work offline, while cloud storage generally requires internet access.
Synchronization: Cloud storage allows data sharing between multiple devices.
Cost: SQLite is generally free, while cloud services may have usage charges.

For example, a notes application can use SQLite to save notes locally and cloud storage to synchronize them across devices.

SQLite is suitable for local data management. Cloud storage is useful for large-scale applications. Both can be combined to provide better performance and data availability.

q: Q80. Evaluate the effectiveness of status bar notifications for communicating background task results.
a:
Status bar notifications are messages displayed by Android applications to inform users about important events and background activities.

Their benefits are:
User Information: Inform users about completed background tasks.
Quick Updates: Display important messages immediately.
User Interaction: Allow users to open an application through notifications.
Task Monitoring: Show download and upload progress.
Convenience: Users can see updates without opening the application.

For example, a field service application can notify an employee when a new work assignment is received.

Developers use Android Notification APIs and NotificationManager to create notifications. They should use proper notification channels and request permission where required. Notifications improve communication and user experience.

q: Q83. Construct a workflow for building, testing, and publishing an Android app on the Play Store.
a:
Publishing an Android application on Google Play Store requires several development and testing steps.

The workflow is:
Requirement Analysis: Identify the purpose and features of the application.
UI Design: Create the application screens.
Development: Write code using Android Studio.
Testing: Check functionality, security and performance.
Bug Fixing: Correct errors found during testing.
Build: Generate a signed Android App Bundle (AAB).
Play Console: Create a Google Play Console developer account.
App Details: Add the application name, description, screenshots and required information.
Submission: Upload the AAB and submit the application for review.
Publishing: Release the application after approval.

This workflow helps developers publish reliable and secure Android applications.

q: Q84. Construct a solution for reading and displaying JSON data from a REST API with error handling.
a:
JSON is a data format used to exchange information between mobile applications and servers. A REST API allows Android applications to collect data from the internet.

The implementation steps are:

Add internet permission in AndroidManifest.xml.

Create an API request using Retrofit or another networking library.

Send an HTTP request to the server.

Receive JSON data as a response.

Convert JSON into Java or Kotlin objects.

Display the information using TextView or RecyclerView.

Handle network errors and invalid responses.

Example JSON: 
{
"name": "Rahul",
"age": 22
}

The application can display the name and age on the screen.

Developers should also handle internet failure, server errors and empty responses. Network operations should run outside the main UI thread.

q: Q85. Design a GPS-based attendance system for field staff using Android.
a:
A GPS-based attendance system is a mobile application that allows field employees to mark attendance using their geographical location.

The main design steps are:
Login: Employees log in using their registered accounts.
GPS Access: The application obtains the employee's current location.
Location Verification: Checks whether the employee is within the permitted workplace area.
Attendance: Records check-in and check-out times.
Database: Stores attendance details on a secure server.
Admin Dashboard: Managers can view employee attendance.
Reports: Generates daily and monthly attendance reports.

For example, a field employee can mark attendance after reaching a customer's location.

The system should use secure authentication, location permissions and server-side verification. It improves attendance management and reduces manual work.

q: Q86. Design a notification system for a field service app using Android notification APIs.
a:
A notification system informs field employees about new tasks, work updates and important activities. Android provides Notification APIs to create and display notifications.

The implementation steps are:
Notification Channel: Create a channel for notifications.
Permission: Request notification permission where required.
Notification Builder: Create a notification using NotificationCompat.Builder.
Notification Manager: Display the notification.
User Action: Open the related screen when the user taps it.
Background Updates: Use Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM) to receive server messages.
Testing: Check notifications on different Android versions.

For example, an employee receives a notification when a manager assigns a new service task.

This system improves communication and helps employees receive important information quickly.
